title: Epic 2: Dependency Security and License Compliance
summary: Epic defining CI dependency vulnerability scanning (cargo audit, OSV-Scanner, Snyk evaluation), cargo deny license policy, and SBOM generation for releases.
notes: MANIFEST_TYPE=DOC applied as authoritative. Document is task/deliverable-structured Epic prose without frontmatter, decision/consequences, user stories, or schemas. Stated policy captured verbatim: Task 2.1 cargo audit required CI check on every PR and main push, build fails on known vulnerabilities with a documented exception process for false positives or unpatched advisories. Task 2.2 OSV-Scanner supplementary, scans Cargo.lock, results as PR annotations. Task 2.3 Snyk free tier to be evaluated; integrate if warranted or document deferral. Task 2.4 deny.toml at repo root: licenses allow MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, Zlib; deny copyleft (GPL, AGPL, LGPL) unless explicitly approved; no banned crates initially; warn on duplicate crate versions; cargo deny check in CI; all current dependencies must pass. Task 2.5 SBOM in release pipeline attached to GitHub releases. Document specifies a single documented exception process for cargo audit advisories and one allow-list license set; it does not enumerate specific advisory IDs, suppression counts, or multiple suppression surfaces, and does not mention .cargo/audit.toml or ci.yml inline ignores.
